title: "Mastermind web"
description: "Owner command center, request authentication, apex-path security design and held Worker publication."
updatedAt: "2026-11-21"
audience: developers

Mastermind is a native TanStack Start + Void + Vite+ Cloudflare Worker in
`apps/mastermind`, served only on `mastermind.tuturuuu.com`. The Worker
rejects `tuturuuu.com/mastermind` and its children, which the gateway
redirects to the dedicated host ([no apex path hosting](#no-apex-path-hosting)).
It does not revive the retired app.

## Command center

### Locale paths

English is the default locale and has no path prefix, like the other
Tuturuuu apps: `/`, `/ship`, `/projects`, `/fleet-access`. Vietnamese keeps
`/vi/...`. The routes use the optional `{-$locale}` segment
(`src/routes/{-$locale}/`), which admits only an absent locale or `vi`. An old
`/en/...` link answers `308` to the same path without the prefix, query kept,
before any session work; a `/en//host` path maps to `/`, never a
protocol-relative `Location`. Sign-in return paths drop the prefix the same
way. Coverage: `src/routes-locale.test.ts` and
`src/native/locale-notice.test.ts`.

`/` (English) and `/vi` (Vietnamese) render the owner command center with
the shared `Structure` shell and `@tuturuuu/ui` components. Every section reads the
[fleet sync](/platform/features/mobile-mastermind#fleet-sync) snapshot, and
nothing renders a value the snapshot does not carry:

- **Today**: the headline counts running lanes and only failures nobody
  picked up again (`counts.failed`); recovered, quota-recovered and cancelled
  lanes appear in a separate "Recovered or cancelled" card with their
  breakdown, beside the list of unsuperseded failed lanes. Four counts:
  running lanes, open items that need the owner, sign-ins waiting, failed.
- **Freshness banner**: `Fleet publisher paused on <machine>` when this page
  still reaches Web but the snapshot's `generatedAt` is old, and "This device
  is offline" when the page's own refresh fails (it shows when the data on
  screen arrived). Live shows when the Mac published and when this browser
  last checked.
- **Inbox**: two lanes. **Needs you** holds open asks, design reviews and
  open sign-in requests, by urgency and then deadline (sign-ins rank with
  high asks). An ask card shows its urgency, requester, countdown, Why now
  and If no answer, numbered options with the recommended one filled, Hold,
  Snooze, and an inline reply steered to the asking lane. Answering moves
  focus to the next card; J and K move, a digit picks that option, R jumps
  to the reply box and Ctrl or Cmd with Enter sends. A tapped answer waits
  five seconds with **Undo**, then shows its delivery state (sending,
  retrying with the same idempotency key, not sent, closed, superseded, or
  the receipt). **FYI** lists open FYI asks and decisions resolved anywhere,
  with "Answered on WhatsApp" (or the phone, the CLI) and "closed here too";
  **Your recent answers** shows each recorded answer as Sent or Received by
  Iris. Snoozed asks sit in a collapsed list under Needs you.
- **Design reviews** (`kind: review`): the preview image, Open full mockup
  (new tab, `noopener`), Approve, and Request changes, which opens a notes
  box and sends `request_changes`. The page never loads a preview URL
  directly: the `loadReviewPreview` server function reads the owner's own
  snapshot, fetches the uploaded asset with the owner's bearer (or a
  first-party hosted image without credentials), refuses redirects, caps the
  size, checks the image signature and returns a data URL, which the page
  CSP (`img-src 'self' data:`) allows. The page reads fleet state with
  `x-mastermind-fleet-features: login,review`.
- **Snooze** is per device: Web keeps no per-owner snooze record, so a snooze
  lives in this browser's storage, hides the ask until the chosen time and
  never changes its deadline or what the phone shows.
- **Access requests**: open requests are answered from Needs you (one card
  per request keeps one answer state); this section keeps closed ones. A
  card shows the allowlisted link, the device code with Copy, the expiry
  countdown, the waiting, approved and verified steps, and "I signed in"
  (the `signed_in` answer). A request whose expiry passes on the page clock
  reads as expired and hides its link and code.
- **Fleet**: the main freeze, production, migrations and incidents strip
  from `release`, then machines with their lanes. Provider quota is not in
  the snapshot, so its card says so.
- **Activity** is built from the snapshot's own timestamps (asks, resolved
  decisions, failed or waiting lanes, incidents, the production deploy).
- **Approvals** tabulates recorded answers and recent resolutions.
- **Cost and health** links to `/admin`; no spend or error budget reaches
  Mastermind. **Notifications** describes the decision push and keeps the
  per-device "Show FYI" switch.

Page state is one union (ready, stale, unpublished, error). A snapshot older
than two minutes, an offline orchestrator or a failed refresh keeps the last
snapshot on screen marked stale and read-only. Regression coverage:
`apps/mastermind/src/components/inbox.test.tsx`,
`src/fleet/inbox-lanes.test.ts` and `src/native/review-preview.test.ts`. The page refreshes every 15 seconds through
TanStack Query; route changes between locales show a fixed skeleton.

## Request admission

The Worker is the only gate: no Cloudflare Access application fronts the host,
and no unsigned header names the user. The session comes from the host cookie
or a Bearer credential, signed for target `mastermind` either way. Tuturuuu Auth, with its MFA, decides who
signed in; the Worker decides what each verified session may open. Every
path, including assets and server functions, passes the Worker first.
Missing configuration fails closed with 503 before storage, API or hub reads.

1. Require HTTPS and exactly `mastermind.tuturuuu.com`.
   Preview and workers.dev hosts are refused regardless of forwarded headers.
2. Verify the satellite access session with
   `TUTURUUU_APP_COORDINATION_SECRET`, target `mastermind`, access scope and a
   maximum lifetime of 300 seconds. Its subject is the actor. The
   request-injected `getSatelliteAppSessionUser` adapter uses shared auth core
   without the legacy helper's database fallback. `Cf-Access-*` and other
   identity headers are ignored.
3. An id in `OWNER_IDS` is the owner. It must carry
   `MASTERMIND_OWNER_EMAIL`, an MFA (aal2) proof that Web signed into the
   session (`mfa`, verified within the last 24 hours and unexpired), and live
   root access on every
   request: `GET /api/v1/mastermind/access` with the owner's session must
   answer `enabled: true` (five-second timeout, redirects refused). Refresh
   carries the proof forward unchanged, so its age bounds how long one
   second-factor check admits the owner. An owner navigation without a
   current MFA proof expires its session cookies and starts the step-up in
   the sign-in itself (`mfaMaxAge=30`): Web hands back a session only with a
   just-verified factor. The `__Host-mastermind_mfa_step` cookie (600
   seconds) marks the step-up, so a session that still lacks MFA afterwards
   gets the notice page instead of another round trip; any other request
   gets a plain 403 notice. Missing or
   empty IDs admit no owner. Session permission scopes are never treated as
   permission evidence, and the owner never falls back to a Fleet grant.
4. Any other subject is a [Fleet grantee](#fleet-access-admission) and reaches
   Fleet paths only.
5. Signed out, `/` and any navigation go to Tuturuuu sign-in through
   `/login`; every other request is a private 403.
6. A navigation the Worker refuses gets a no-script notice page in the
   path's locale with the one step that fixes it, never a bare `Forbidden`:
   a sign-in callback that cannot finish offers `/login` again for the same
   page, and a signed-in account without access offers
   `/login?account=choose`, which asks Web for its account picker
   (`confirmAccount=1`). Every other refused request stays a plain 403.

### Fleet access admission

A person with a live Fleet grant opens only the
[Fleet area](/platform/features/fleet-access#mastermind-web). Every other path
and method answers 403 before any session refresh, permission check or render,
with no login redirect. The admitted requests are exactly:

- `GET /fleet-access` or `/vi/fleet-access` (no `HEAD`);
- `GET /assets/*` (no `HEAD`);
- `GET` or same-origin `POST /_serverFn/fleet-access.<name>` for the six
  functions in `src/fleet-access/api.ts`.

`/login` and `/verify-token` run before this gate, because a grantee needs
them to get a session. The subject decides the return: `/verify-token` uses
the subject Web verified, and `/login` the subject of a session the browser
already holds. For a grantee both return only to the Fleet page: any other
`nextUrl` becomes `/fleet-access`. Before any refresh, the subject of the
access session (or, once it expires, of the refresh credential) is read from
local signature checks, so a grantee on another path is refused without a
network call.

Production builds give a server function the SHA-256 of
`<root-relative file>--<variable>_createServerFn_handler`. The Vite config's
`generateFunctionId` receives exactly those inputs and pins
`fleet-access.<variable>` only for `src/fleet-access/api.ts` and the exports
listed in `src/native/fleet-admission.ts`; the Worker matches those IDs
exactly. The command center's functions keep hashed IDs and stay owner-only. A
test fails when `api.ts` exports a function the list does not name.

Each Fleet request rechecks `GET /api/v1/fleet/access` with the grantee's
session. Only `enabled: true`, `stopped: false` and an Observer, Steerer or
Operator tier admit: the Fleet API answers the configured Owner with tier
`owner` and no grant row, so that answer never admits. An id in `OWNER_IDS`
never takes the grantee path, and session issuance and refresh apply the same
rules. There is no memo: a revoked or stopped grant denies the next request,
and a failed or redirected check denies. The request context sets a Fleet
actor for every role but the owner identity only for the owner, so
`currentOwner()` throws for a grantee. The Fleet API checks the live grant
again on every read and write.

**Emitted-Worker coverage.** `native-built-worker.acceptance.mjs` runs the
cases in `fleet-admission.acceptance-cases.mjs` on the same sealed Worker, in
CI only (`bun run test:runtime` in `mastermind-cloudflare.yaml`, after the
artifact is sealed). They render the Fleet page in both locales without the
command center loader, call all six pinned IDs with the grantee session and
require each to reach its Fleet API route, prove the owner's hashed
`loadFleet` ID is real for the owner and denied to the grantee, deny the owner
routes and `HEAD`, and deny the Owner tier and a revoked grant.

**Granting.** A Fleet grant on Tuturuuu is the whole grant: there is no
second allowlist at the edge. **Offboarding.** Revoke the Fleet grant; the
next request is denied, and the next refresh with it.

## Session issuance

`mastermind` is a registered internal app on `https://mastermind.tuturuuu.com`
only (`PRODUCTION_INTERNAL_APP_DOMAINS`), so the central login hands off to it
like every other satellite. No other host, subdomain or path maps to it.

1. A navigation without a valid session goes to
   `/login`, which answers 303 to `https://tuturuuu.com/login` with
   `returnUrl=https://mastermind.tuturuuu.com/verify-token?nextUrl=<path>`.
   Return paths must stay on the host and never point at `/login` or
   `/verify-token`. `/login` also stores a random nonce and a PKCE verifier
   in the `__Host-mastermind_login_state` cookie (600 seconds). The Worker
   signs the S256 challenge, callback, expiry and MFA intent in the return
   URL. When the browser carries a central
   Tuturuuu session cookie (a routing hint only), the same query goes to
   Web's [signed-in continue](/platform/architecture/authentication#signed-in-continue-for-first-party-apps)
   instead, which returns straight to `/verify-token` without rendering the
   sign-in page; a step-up (`mfa=fresh`) or an account choice always uses
   `/login`.
2. Web checks the signed transaction and its own MFA policy. The login
   page's fetch can check the account and MFA and receive a navigation URL.
   Only an unprefetched top-level document navigation claims the transaction
   in the replay store and mints a single-use, 300-second `mastermind`
   token bound to the Worker's challenge. `/verify-token` checks the nonce
   against the cookie and presents the verifier, the Worker-only redeem
   proof, and Web's token-specific issuer proof to
   `POST /api/v1/auth/cross-app-token/verify`. Web redeems it only through the service-role
   PKCE validator, so a handoff URL copied from history or logs cannot be
   redeemed from another browser. The Worker accepts the answer only when
   the access and refresh tokens verify locally for target `mastermind` and
   name the same subject, and the access session lives at most 300 seconds.
   An owner id must carry the owner email; any other subject's new session
   must hold a live Fleet grant. Web's handoff enforces the account's MFA
   policy, and its MFA proof travels in the session for the owner check.
3. Both credentials are set host-only (no `Domain`), `Path=/`, `HttpOnly`,
   `Secure`, `SameSite=Lax`, and the owner returns to the path.
4. When the access session expires, the next request sends the refresh
   credential to `POST /api/v1/auth/cross-app-session/refresh` (after verifying
   it locally; an owner id needs the owner email), accepts only a session for
   that same subject (a grantee's only with a live grant), renders with it and
   sets
   the rotated cookies on that response. Web's replay grace covers concurrent
   requests. A non-navigation without a session is 403.

`FIXED_INTERNAL_APP_SESSION_CAPS` in `@tuturuuu/auth/app-session-policy` caps
Mastermind at a 300-second access session, a 60-second refresh-early window
and a one-day refresh credential. The resolver and `createAppSessionTokenPair`
both apply it, so no `APP_COORDINATION_SESSION_POLICY` value can loosen it.
`mastermind` is not in `ALL_SATELLITE_APP_SESSION_TARGETS`: its session opens
only the routes that name it (`/api/v1/mastermind/access`, fleet state and
answers). `OWNER_ONLY_INTERNAL_APPS` (`@tuturuuu/utils/owner-only-apps`) keeps
it out of the credentialed accounts CORS origins and API cost identity. The
database audience `private.cross_app_internal_app_names()` lists it
(migration `20261121123000_mastermind_cross_app_token_audience`).

**Worker-only redemption.** Web's verify and refresh routes redeem a
`mastermind` handoff token or refresh credential only with the
`x-tuturuuu-app-redeem-proof` header: an HMAC-SHA256 of the target and the
credential under the coordination secret (`@tuturuuu/auth/app-redeem-proof`;
any current or next secret verifies). Only the Worker and Web hold that
secret, so no other client can redeem them directly. The Worker rejects a
refresh credential that lives longer than a day and a handoff token that is
not 64 lowercase hex characters, without calling Web. A refresh cookie lifted
from the browser still works when replayed to the Worker, so the owner's
24-hour MFA age is what ends a stolen chain.

**Login state.** `/login` sets a random `__Host-mastermind_login_state` cookie
(`__Host-` so no sibling subdomain can plant it, `Path=/`, ten minutes, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax`)
and carries the same value as `mm_state` inside `nextUrl`, the only part of
the return Web keeps. `/verify-token` exchanges a handoff only when both
match, strips `mm_state` from the return and clears the cookie, so a handoff
URL started in another browser cannot sign this browser in as someone else.

The session cookies carry `__Host-` names too (`__Host-mastermind_session`,
`__Host-mastermind_refresh`). The Worker drops the shared app-session cookie
names before verifying, so a session a sibling `*.tuturuuu.com` host plants
under those names is never read.

Deploy the Mastermind Worker with transaction signing and issuer-proof
forwarding before activating the new Web issuer and redemption routes.
Web enforces both only with `MASTERMIND_SIGNIN_TRANSACTION_REQUIRED=true`
(off by default). While it is off, Web still verifies any transaction or
issuer proof it receives and refuses a return whose transaction is invalid,
but a return without one keeps the earlier PKCE handoff, so the serving
Worker can sign in during the overlap. Turn it on only after the signing
Worker serves; turning it off is the rollback.
Start a fresh sign-in from Mastermind when a transaction expires or was
already used. Regression tests cover unsigned requests, callback changes,
browser fetch, prefetch, concurrent replay, and tokens missing Web issuer proof.

**Revocation.** Removing the owner from the Worker's `OWNER_IDS` or from
Web's root Mastermind permission denies the next request and every refresh.
Revoking a Fleet grant denies the grantee's next request and refresh. Signing
out of Tuturuuu ends Web's session but not the Worker's: each refresh rotates
a new one-day credential, so the chain continues while it is used daily. The
owner's chain stops admitting 24 hours after the second-factor check it
carries; a grantee's chain ends with the grant. An access session already
issued stays valid at the Web fleet routes until it expires, at most 300
seconds.

## Data boundaries and memo

Data moves only through two server functions, `loadFleet` (GET) and
`answerFleetDecision` (POST), which run after every admission gate and read
the owner from the request context. `createFleetClient` calls
`GET /api/v1/mastermind/fleet/state` (with
`x-mastermind-fleet-features: login,review`) and
`POST /api/v1/mastermind/fleet/decisions/{id}/answer` with only the owner's
satellite bearer, refuses redirects, applies an eight-second timeout and
validates every body against the shared contract in
`apps/web/src/lib/mastermind/fleet`. Those Web routes admit the Mastermind
satellite session (target `mastermind`, scope `internal-app:session`) next
to the Web session; the owner allowlist and root permission still apply.
The browser never calls an app API directly. The uncalled ops-hub and org
scaffolds keep their constraints: replace the hub stub with the gateway HMAC
assertion path and pass C1 API acceptance before use. There is no second
person store.

The memo factory is per-isolate, keyed by owner ID, bounded to 32 entries and
expires after 60 seconds or session expiry. Run authentication and the owner
gate before consulting it. Removing an owner from the request environment
revokes immediately. A future live permission memo must preserve the same
maximum revocation window and test real permission removal with C1.
All responses are `private, no-store`; no people data may use edge caches.

## Security and verification

After admission, GET and HEAD pass; POST passes only under the app's
`_serverFn/` base with `Origin` equal to the request origin and
`Sec-Fetch-Site` absent or `same-origin`. Every other method or path is 405.
Start's CSRF middleware checks server functions again.

The Worker creates a 128-bit nonce per response. The router (`ssr.nonce`),
the base head script and the theme script stamp it on every script, and the
policy is `script-src 'nonce-…' 'strict-dynamic'` with `style-src 'self'`,
`object-src 'none'`, `base-uri 'none'`, `form-action 'self'` and
`frame-ancestors 'none'`; there is no `unsafe-inline`. Responses without a
document run no scripts. Server-rendered `style` attributes are refused, so
`Structure`'s width variables come from `.mastermind-shell` in the app
stylesheet, and menus are non-modal so no scroll-lock stylesheet is injected.
HSTS, nosniff, DENY and no-referrer apply to denied responses too.

On an admitted host run
`ttr resources run -- bun run --cwd apps/mastermind test`.
The matrix signs real JWTs and app sessions and asserts 403 with zero reads.
It also checks JWKS fetch failure, unknown keys, rotation after cooldown,
apex-path refusal and the POST method gate. It covers immediate owner revocation, memo expiry and isolation, user-credential
forwarding and a recursive privileged-key-name scan.
The owning native workflow builds in CI, then seals and restores the Worker.
Its explicit test:runtime command runs the .acceptance.mjs suite against the
emitted artifact; generic source-test discovery must not run that suite. The
suite serves a synthetic fleet snapshot, renders both locales and requires
every `<script>` to carry the response's CSP nonce, a fresh nonce per
response, and 405 for a cross-site server-function POST. Runtime
fixtures use isolated .invalid preview hosts. The source auth matrix also checks
the production-like preview hostname.
The local emitted-Worker fixture sets `dev.origin.secure: true` while its
listener remains on loopback HTTP. The runner otherwise rewrites HTTPS inputs to
HTTP before the Worker sees them, and the required HTTPS guard correctly denies
the owner before JWT verification. Preserve the hostname without an origin-host
override so preview and apex hosts still fail. The source matrix separately
asserts that a plaintext HTTP owner request returns 403 with zero reads.

## No apex path hosting

Mastermind is served only on `mastermind.tuturuuu.com`. With
`GATEWAY_MASTERMIND_REDIRECT=1`, which the release owner sets on the gateway
once the host passes acceptance, the gateway answers `tuturuuu.com/mastermind`
and its children with a plain 302 to it (path suffix and query kept, no
proxying). The build is pinned to the root
(`basePath: ''`). Mounting it on the shared `tuturuuu.com` origin was
reviewed and rejected, because nothing can bind the caller there:

- Every Web page is same-origin with the mount. A Web script can set
  `referrer` to a `/mastermind` URL, `history.pushState` there, or
  `window.open('/mastermind/…')` and script the opened document, so
  `Sec-Fetch-Site`, a `Referer` path, a CSRF token read from the page and a
  double-submit cookie all pass. GET server functions (`loadFleet`) would
  also return the snapshot, login links and device codes to that script.
- A session derived from the shared root session makes every same-origin
  request carrying it the owner. Cookie isolation (`isolation` in the mount
  config, which the Worker never applies today) would still forward an
  access-token-only Supabase session.
- An Access path application only proves Access passed the request: a Web
  page's fetch of `/mastermind/*` carries `CF_Authorization` and receives a
  real assertion. Its defaults are domain-scoped, readable by script and
  `SameSite=None`.
- `localStorage` is per origin, and Web's service worker (scope `/`) would
  intercept the mount.

Any future proposal must survive a real-browser matrix with the owner signed
in: Web-page GET and POST to both server functions (also after `pushState`,
with a forged `referrer` and from a `window.open` opener) return 403 with no
snapshot data and zero upstream calls; framing is refused; the service
worker never answers the mount; `CF_Authorization` is `Path=/mastermind`,
`HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Strict` and absent from `/` and `/api/`; AUDs
are per host; the app-visible cookies hold no Web, app or Supabase session;
and owner removal is immediate.

## Production release

`productionPublicationPolicy.mastermind` admits the `tuturuuu-mastermind`
Worker for `mastermind.tuturuuu.com` only; `workers_dev` and preview URLs
stay off and the source declares no routes. A production sync that touches
the app (or the shared fleet contract) calls `mastermind-cloudflare.yaml` on
the `production` ref:

1. `artifact` builds once, seals the archive and runs the emitted-Worker
   acceptance for that exact commit.
2. `production-policy` evaluates the publication policy; deleting or
   holding the entry stops every later write.
3. `deploy` (GitHub environment `mastermind-production`, secret
   `MASTERMIND_CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`) restores and re-verifies the sealed
   archive, converts it to cf Build Output without rebuilding and requires the
   Worker secret names `MASTERMIND_OWNER_EMAIL`, `OWNER_IDS` and
   `TUTURUUU_APP_COORDINATION_SECRET`.
   Holding the deploy slot, it publishes only when the run's commit is still
   the `production` head, so a rerun of an older run publishes nothing. It
   captures the serving version, uploads the new one, records its id, checks
   the head again, and moves traffic only while the captured version still
   serves; a run overtaken during upload leaves its version without traffic. The first
   release creates the Worker, which answers 503 until its secrets exist.
4. With `MASTERMIND_HOST_ATTACHED=true`, the job checks the sign-in gate
   anonymously: `/` answers 303 to `/login`, `/login` answers 303 to
   Tuturuuu sign-in with the `/verify-token` return, and the locales,
   `/verify-token`, a server function, an asset and `/api/build-info` answer
   a private 403. While `MASTERMIND_ACCESS_TEAM_DOMAIN` is set (an Access
   application still fronting the host), it instead requires every path to
   redirect to that team's Access login. After any
   failure the captured version is assigned back only while this run's own
   version is serving. Receipts are kept for 30 days. A deployment marker is
   recorded only for an existing, configured Worker whose host check passed;
   the owner's signed-in acceptance on the live host stays a manual gate.

The planner calls the workflow (`deploy-mastermind-cloudflare`) when a
production sync changes its inputs, and looks up its marker like the other
Cloudflare targets. Until the first marker exists, release explicitly with
`gh workflow run mastermind-cloudflare.yaml --ref production`.

Traffic changes are serialized by the deploy concurrency group, and each
assignment re-reads the serving version first (`--expect-current`). Run a
manual assignment only while no release run is in progress, so an operator
change and a workflow rollback never race.

Manual rollback is one step:
`node scripts/ci/void-cf-publisher.mjs assign --worker tuturuuu-mastermind --version <previous version id>`
with the version from the run's `mastermind-release-*` receipt.

Provisioned outside the source, by name: the Worker custom domain
`mastermind.tuturuuu.com` (DNS), the three Worker secrets, the
`mastermind-production` environment with `MASTERMIND_CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`,
the variable `MASTERMIND_HOST_ATTACHED` and, on the gateway,
`GATEWAY_MASTERMIND_REDIRECT`. No Cloudflare Access application covers the
host: Tuturuuu Auth, with MFA, is the only sign-in, so Access would only add a
second login without adding an authority the Worker lacks.

A real-browser smoke that loads, refreshes and answers through the compiled
server functions, MFA and live permission acceptance, and the revocation
checks run on the live host before the gateway redirect is enabled.
Follow the [native Start runbook](/build/devops/native-start-migration).
